summary: Tenant-scoped session cookie prefixing removes tenant claim, blocking admin impersonation (403)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that admin impersonation requests to the admin-ops endpoint are returning 403 when performed from their tenant admin console. The failure started after a proxy upgrade in the customer's private deployment. Impact: admins cannot impersonate users in tenant-scoped environments, blocking support and admin workflows for multiple teams at the customer.

Impact:
- Nimbus Health admins unable to impersonate users via /admin/impersonate (403).
- Operational impact: blocked troubleshooting and support actions for ~10 teams, estimated >2 hours/day lost productivity.
- Risk: escalation to enterprise support if not resolved within 48 hours.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) running across us-west-2 region.
- Identity stack: identity-proxy v1.12.0 (customer installed), auth-service v2.3.1, api-gateway v3.0.0.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Login as tenant admin to customer console (tenant ID: tenant-nimbus-43).
2) Open impersonation UI and attempt to impersonate a standard user.
3) Observe network request to https://api.private.nimbus.example/admin/impersonate returns 403.
4) Capture request/response headers and auth cookie.

Observed logs and headers (redacted):
- Response: 403 Forbidden {"error":"forbidden","reason":"missing_tenant_claim"}
- auth cookie: "rw_session=eyJhbGciOi..." (cookie name prefixed by "__Tenant_tenant-nimbus-43_rw_session")
- identity-proxy access log: trace_id=trc-7b2a9c, upstream_status=403, upstream_error="rbac: tenant claim not present"

Notes: The cookie name is being rewritten/prefixed at the edge to include the tenant scope (pattern __Tenant_<tenantid>_<cookie>). The RBAC layer expects an "org_id" claim in the session JWT payload. We see the JWT payload on the proxy decode contains no "org_id" claim, whereas the original session token prior to proxy rewrite included org_id.

Additional context:
- Customer recently upgraded their ingress edge component (third-party CDN/proxy) which inserts a cookie-name prefix to isolate cookies between tenants.
- This prefixing step also triggers a code path in our identity-proxy which attempts to normalize cookie names and, due to a race in header parsing, strips a small Base64 chunk from the cookie value for some prefixes. That truncated value decodes to a JWT missing the org_id claim (signature still valid).

Expected behavior:
- Cookie-name prefixing by external proxies should not modify cookie value bytes. identity-proxy should correctly locate and decode the full session token and preserve claims including org_id.

Workarounds attempted:
- Customer temporarily disabled cookie-name prefixing at the edge and impersonation succeeded immediately.
- Support suggested passing tenant id via X-Forwarded-Tenant header; customer cannot enable that pattern in their CDN.

Action requested:
- Investigate and provide code fix and backported patch for identity-proxy to avoid truncation when cookie names include tenant prefixes, add unit and integration tests covering prefixed cookie names, and provide a recommended patched binary for the customer's private deployment.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Authenticate as tenant admin for tenant-nimbus-43 on customer's private deployment.
2) Trigger POST /admin/impersonate with target user id.
3) Observe 403 and check identity-proxy access log for trace_id trc-7b2a9c.
4) Compare cookie value before and after edge prefixing (if accessible) or disable prefixing to confirm behavior.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: edge prefixing mutated cookie name only; however reproduction shows cookie value truncated in a deterministic way when prefix includes tenant pattern. Team reproduced locally by adding prefix to cookie name and confirmed identity-proxy v1.12.0 normalization routine was using fixed-offset substring logic that mis-calculated start index when prefix length exceeded 12 chars. Eng (Marco) added debug logs and confirmed trim logic triggered. Related internal ticket INT-4421 tracks normalization rewrite from 2025 which introduced the bug.

- Repro on dev: yes (added integration test).
- Root cause: cookie-name normalization routine in identity-proxy uses brittle offset math when splitting name by underscores. When cookie name contains additional underscores from tenant prefix, normalization logic treated part of the cookie value as name separator and sliced the value buffer incorrectly.

Work for fix:
- Replace substring arithmetic with explicit parsing using lastIndexOf and boundary checks.
- Add test cases for prefixes with multiple underscores and long tenant ids.
- Prepare backport to v1.11.x and patch for v1.12.0.

Links: Slack thread #support (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05SUPP123/p1650000000000000), runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SUPPORT/tenant-cookie-scope-runbook, internal ticket INT-4421.
comments: Support (Aisha): Opened with customer-reported 403 on impersonation endpoint. Attached proxy logs and customer-captured cookie samples.
Customer (N. Harris, Nimbus Health): Confirmed issue began after their CDN upgrade last night. They can reproduce consistently and provided a dump of the original cookie before the CDN rewrites it.

Eng (Marco Diaz): Reproduced locally with prefixed cookie name; identity-proxy normalization routine uses fixed offsets. Preparing patch and unit tests. Blocking: need a signed backport approval for release to private deployments.
Support (Aisha): Customer requested ETA for patch and whether a hotfix binary is available. Provided temporary mitigation instructions to disable cookie prefixing and noted potential deploy window.
Eng (Marco Diaz): Patch ready in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1234. Will prepare backport PR to v1.11.x and coordinate with Release for a security-style hotfix release.
Support (Aisha): Communicated to customer that hotfix will be available and asked for preferred maintenance window. Customer requested ASAP — they will accept off-hours deploy tonight.
resolution: Fix implemented in identity-proxy: replaced brittle substring logic with robust parsing using lastIndexOf and explicit boundary checks. Backported patch applied to v1.11.x and v1.12.0 branch. Release artifacts published and hotfix binary provided to customer. Added unit and integration tests for prefixed cookie names and tenant ids containing underscores.
resolution_notes:
- PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1234
- Backport PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1240
- Hotfix binary delivered to Nimbus Health and applied to their private cluster on 2026-03-11 22:30 UTC by their infra team.
- Post-deploy validation: impersonation requests succeeded, no more 403s observed.
- Follow-up: Add monitoring alert to detect JWT payloads missing org_id claim and a dashboard to track impersonation success rate per-tenant.
- Customer confirmed closure and requested a short postmortem; follow-up action: Support to provide one within 3 business days.
